scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Wolosso arose in 2006 in Ivory Coast as a popular dance style that rapidly spread throughout West Africa.
Historically, the style represents a synthesis of traditional African folk dances and Western pop dance culture.
on_screen: Map: Ivory Coast · Africa
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance functions as a contemporary social dance.
In predominantly Muslim countries of West Africa, Wolosso has stirred strong public offense due to movements perceived as lascivious.
Stripped of their original ritual and folk contexts, these bodily articulations are frequently identified with decadent Western culture.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: AFRICA DANCE 5 (2005) – 24 CLIPS | Compilation Africaine – DVD COMPLET (https://archive.org/details/africa-dance-5-complet)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed through isolated circular hip movements.
Female dancers periodically lower the upper body, placing heavy emphasis on the buttocks.
The movement operates over an offbeat-accented 4/4 meter, at moderate to fast musical pacing between 40 and 70 bpm.
Watch for Isolated hip roll, Torso drop accent.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (pR9RHZGLat0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Social dance floor or urban space

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance relies on an offbeat-emphasized 4/4 rhythm that is often layered with polyrhythmic counters typical of African folk traditions.
The musical tempo is positioned between 40 and 70 bpm.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 55 beats a minute.

Characterized by an offbeat-accented 4/4 beat operating at a deliberate tempo between 40 and 70 bpm, overlaid with complex polyrhythmic counters characteristic of African popular and folk music traditions.

narration: Count: 1-2-3-4 then 5-6-7-8 (eight counts, two bars). The meter is 4/4.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer

Step 4: Lower the torso forward while maintaining the rolling hip circles to emphasize the buttocks

scenes.title: Put it together

Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Standing stationary hip isolations left and right
